question: Hoysaleswara Temple is located in which of the following states?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hoysaleswara temple** is also referred simply to as the Halebidu temple.

 
 
• It is a 12th-century Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva.
 
• **Hoysaleswara architecture is the Hindu temple architecture which got developed in the region of Karnataka near Mysore**__.
 
• It was built between 1121 AD and 1160 AD in the region of Halebid, then known as Dorasamudra, which was the capital of the Hoysalas.
 
• It was built on the banks of a large man-made lake.
 
• It is famous for sculptures and architecture from the Hoysala period.
 
• It was also built during the reign of Vishnuvardhana.
 
• The temple is Dwikuta, which means two temples called **"Hoysaleshwar" and "Shantleeshwar"**.
 __
 
• Shantala was the queen of Vishnuvardhana.
 
 
 
• It was built to compete with the Chennakeshava temple which was under construction as a Vaishnava temple.
 
• Hoysaleshwara Temple is surrounded by ponds, mandapas and lakes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Hoysala Empire** and its capital Dorasamudra were invaded, plundered, and destroyed in the early 14th century by the Delhi Sultanate armies of Alauddin Khilji.

 
 
• The Hoysala was built around 1500 temples at 958 centers between 1000 AD to 1346 AD.
 
 
• The finest temples were commissioned during the times of Vishnuvardhana.
 
 
 
• The Hoysala temple architecture was heavily influenced by the Western Chalukyas, Cholas as well as Pallavas, though there was a departure from the Chalukyan style.
